\begin{bankq}[id=SI01-P1-PHY-S2-Q09, source={Score-I - Test 01 (16 Jun 2021)}, paper=1, qno=9, type=multi, subtopic={Pendulums}, answer={A,C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: stick pivoted on a frictionless table struck by a particle | steps: angular momentum about pivot; collision elastic condition; centre of percussion; check options}]
A uniform stick with mass $m$ and length $\ell$ lies on a frictionless horizontal surface. It is pivoted at a point a distance $x$ from centre. A spring (at its relaxed length) with spring constant $k$ is attached to the far end of the stick, perpendicular to the stick, as shown. Stick is given a small kick, then:
\bfig{83.4}{SI01_p1_phy_s2_q09_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Value of $x$ which yields largest frequency of oscillation is $\dfrac{\ell}{3}$.}
\opt{B}{Value of $x$ which yields largest frequency of oscillation is $\dfrac{\ell}{6}$.}
\opt{C}{Angular frequency of oscillation (largest value) is $\dfrac{2k}{m}$.}
\opt{D}{Angular frequency of oscillation (largest value) is $\dfrac{4k}{m}$.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\opt{D}{pressure on the base of a container containing liquid.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SII03-P1-PHY-S1-Q02, source={Score-II - Test 03 (05 May 2021)}, paper=1, qno=2, type=single, subtopic={Damped and forced oscillations}, answer={C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=3, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C0 F0}, diff_note={concepts: damping coefficient of a driven oscillator | steps: driving force in phase with velocity at resonance; F0 = gamma times velocity amplitude; gamma = F0/(x0 omega)}]

\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\dfrac{F_o}{x_o\omega}$}
\opt{B}{$\dfrac{F_o}{2x_o\omega}$}
\opt{C}{$\dfrac{F_o}{mx_o\omega}$}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac{F_o}{2mx_o\omega}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SA06-P2-PHY-S2-Q10, source={Score Advanced - Test 06 (04 Sep 2021)}, paper=2, qno=10, type=single, subtopic={Spring-mass}, answer={A}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: phase space diagrams of oscillators | steps: phase trajectory shapes; energy contour; match}]
Phase space diagrams are useful tools in analyzing all kinds of dynamical problems. They are especially useful in studying the changes in motion as initial position and momentum are changed. Here we consider some simple dynamical systems for which phase space is a plane in which position is plotted along horizontal axis and momentum is plotted along vertical axis. The phase space diagram is x(t) vs. p(t) curve in this plane. The arrow on the curve indicates the time flow. For example, the phase space diagram for a particle moving with constant velocity is a straight line as shown in the figure. Similarly we may also plot momentum of a pendulum versus $\theta$ (with sign convention shown in figure (b)).\par
\bfig{78.7}{SA06_p2_phy_s2_q10_1.png}
Figure (b) shows phase diagram of motion of simple pendulum (momentum P versus angle $\theta$). Choose potential energy level at the lowest point of the pendulum. E represents total energy of simple pendulum. Pendulum has a point mass connected with light rod.\par
\bfig{236.8}{SA06_p2_phy_s2_q10_2.png}

\hline
\multicolumn{2}{|c|}{List-I} & \multicolumn{2}{c|}{List-II} \\ \hline
(P) & Phase diagram a & (1) & E $<$ 2 mg$\ell$ \\ \hline
(Q) & Phase diagram b & (2) & E $\geq$ 2mg$\ell$ \\ \hline
(R) & Phase diagram c & (3) & May perform periodic and oscillatory motion \\ \hline
(S) & Phase diagram d & (4) & May represent SHM \\ \hline
 & & (5) & May represent angular velocity $\omega$ versus $\theta$ for a pendulum bob \\ \hline
\end{tabular}}\par

\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=NUR04-P1-PHY-S2-Q11, source={Nurture (General) - Test 04 (11 Feb 2024)}, paper=1, qno=11, type=multi, subtopic={Spring-mass}, answer={A,B}, answer_src=solved, working={Putty at the mean position conserves momentum; at an end point the amplitude is unchanged}, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: putty dropped on an oscillating block, spring-mass | steps: momentum at the mean position; new amplitude; end point case; period}]
A block with mass M attached to a horizontal spring with force constant k is moving with simple harmonic motion having amplitude $A_1$. At the instant when the block passes through its equilibrium position a lump of putty with mass m is dropped vertically on the block from a very small height and sticks to it.
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The new amplitude is $A_2=A_1\sqrt{\dfrac M{M+m}}$}
\opt{B}{Time period will be $T_2=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{M+m}k}$}
\opt{C}{For the case in which the putty is dropped on the block when it is at one end of its path, the new amplitude $A_2=A_1\sqrt{\dfrac m{m+M}}$}
\opt{D}{For the case in which the putty is dropped on the block when it is at one end of its path, the new Time period will be $T_2=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m+M}{2K}}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
